item.title: Stinkbug Leg Organ Hosts Symbiotic Fungi That Protect Eggs from Parasitic Wasps
item.description:
📝 This fungal symbiosis is far from a passive association; it represents an active, evolved mechanism whereby female stinkbugs coat their freshly laid eggs with a living fungal shield. However, the fungal hyphae emanating from the leg organ form a physical barrier that deters such parasitism. This symbiotic system holds remarkable evolutionary significance.
🔗 Read more: https://bioengineer.org/stinkbug-leg-organ-hosts-symbiotic-fungi-that-protect-eggs-from-parasitic-wasps/
